A split-panel illustration. On the left side (Amos' time), wealthy merchants in luxurious robes are shown using a rigged weighing scale to cheat a poor, barefoot farmer out of his grain. On the right side (James' teaching), a modern Christian believer is shown kindly handing bags of groceries and supplies to a widow and her young children in a humble home.

A marketplace scene in ancient Israel. Hosea, looking compassionate and resolute, is handing a pouch of silver coins and pointing to a large basket of barley held by a merchant. In front of them stands Gomer, looking down in shame and poverty. The scene captures the moment of Hosea buying back his unfaithful wife, a symbol of God's redemptive love.
